summary: Portable 3LCD XGA projector field reference covering identification, placement, power, I/O, consumables, intake, and source confidence.

sections.title: Identification
sections.lede: The badge on the chassis rarely matches what you will search for. All three names are the same hardware.
rows: S39 / W39 / X39 family — one shared user's guide

notes.label: Searching for parts
notes.text: Search PowerLite X39 in the US and EB-X39 everywhere else. EX39 alone returns mostly resale listings, not documentation. The user's guide is filed under the S39/W39/X39 series.

sections.title: Optical & image
rows: 0.55 in with MLA (micro lens array), D10 generation
Accepts up to 1080p, scaled to XGA
3,500 lumens white and color light output (ISO 21118)

notes.label: Why the equal-lumen figure matters
notes.text: Color light output equals white light output at 3,500 lumens, a 3LCD trait. That makes slides, charts, and saturated graphics look stronger than the headline number alone suggests.

sections.title: Throw & placement
sections.lede: Throw ratio 1.48–1.77:1. Wide means closer placement or a larger image; Tele means farther placement or a smaller image. The 1.2× zoom fills everything between.

cards.label: Rule of thumb
cards.text: Screen width in feet × 1.5 puts you near the wide end. Fine-tune with zoom.

cards.label: Total range
cards.text: 0.89–10.95 m lens-to-screen across the full 30–300 in image range.

cards.label: Offset
cards.text: No lens shift. Plan the table height instead of correcting placement with keystone.

sections.caption: Official projection distances, 4:3 — Epson PowerLite S39/W39/X39 User's Guide

notes.label: Reading the offset
notes.text: Offset is measured from lens center to the bottom edge of the image. Negative means the image begins below lens center for table mounting; ceiling mounting flips the relationship.

sections.title: Lamp
rows: Lamp cover on top of the chassis
paragraphs: ECO mode doubles rated lamp life and cuts fan noise by 9 dB. Unless the room demands the full 3,500 lumens, ECO is the better default.

sections.title: Power draw
sections.lede: Published figures differ between Epson's US spec sheet and Epson Europe's EB-X39 data. Size any power source against the higher number.

notes.label: The number that decides battery use
notes.text: Normal mode exceeds 300 W under every published source; ECO sits below it. A 300 W-limited source can support steady ECO draw but cannot support Normal, and lamp-strike surge still matters.

sections.title: ECO mode / battery
sections.lede: Set ECO before moving to a limited-wattage source. The startup sequence may demand Normal-mode power before the menu is reachable.
paragraphs: The setting is expected to persist across power cycles until changed or Reset All is performed. A leaf icon identifies active power-saving settings. High-altitude mode or high ambient temperature may limit the option; persistence should be verified on the unit.
sections.subheading: First start on a limited-wattage source
steps: Power the projector from a wall outlet that can supply Normal mode, about 330 W.
Set Power Consumption to ECO using the menu path above.
Power off fully and let the cool-down cycle finish. Do not pull the plug mid-fan.
Connect the battery pack and power on. Confirm the unit remains in ECO.

notes.label: If it trips the pack anyway
notes.text: Lamp strike can exceed steady-state draw. A pack rated at exactly 300 W continuous with no surge headroom may still cut out at ignition. Check the surge rating.

sections.title: Consumables
paragraphs: Prices are 2026 street estimates for a discontinued product and will drift. Replace or clean the air filter whenever the lamp is changed.

sections.title: Intake checklist
sections.lede: Run this on any used unit before it is committed to a job.

items.title: Read lamp hours
items.detail: Menu → Info → Lamp Hours. Compare with 6,000 h Normal / 12,000 h ECO.

items.title: Confirm clean startup
items.detail: Image appears and no warning indicators remain on the control panel.

items.title: Check for even brightness
items.detail: Use a full white field. Look for colored blobs, dim corners, or a yellow-green cast.

items.title: Test the inputs you will use
items.detail: At minimum test HDMI. Inspect used VGA ports for bent pins.

items.title: Exercise focus and both keystone axes
items.detail: Confirm the focus ring travels smoothly and the horizontal slider is not seized.

items.title: Run for ten minutes and listen
items.detail: The fan should settle to a steady tone without rattling or cyclical whine.

items.title: Clean filter and lens
items.detail: Do this before the first real job, not after a thermal shutdown.

items.title: Set ECO for battery use
items.detail: Follow section 07 on wall power before connecting a limited-wattage battery.

cards.label: Aspect ratio
cards.text: Native 4:3. Widescreen content letterboxes into roughly 1024×576 usable pixels.

cards.label: Color
cards.text: Equal white and color output makes the unit strong for slides, charts, and saturated graphics.

cards.label: Best use
cards.text: Portable business or classroom projection, or a backup unit where some ambient light remains.

cards.label: Network features
cards.text: LAN projection, USB Display, and RS-232 control remain useful for multi-presenter setups.
